precedents.note: Both applicants are single defense contractor employees whose security clearance cases rest on the same Government concern about financial decisions and reliability, and both have delinquent debts appearing on credit reports and admitted in the SOR responses. The precedent's applicant admitted three delinquent debts, while the case under review involves 23 alleged debts with student loans among them.

Both applicants work for a defense contractor and have delinquent student loans, with one applicant unable to identify which institution holds them and the other unsure who holds his loans. Both also have unpaid medical debts, and each could not verify or locate the creditor for at least one of them.

Both applicants are single, hold bachelor's degrees from 2009, and are alleged under the same financial-decision concern about poor self-control, judgment, and rule compliance, with the government alleging delinquent student loans in each case. Both involve delinquent student loan debt as a central part of the alleged indebtedness.

Both applicants hold security clearance cases with the same Government concern about financial decisions and reliability, and both report delinquent debts that appeared on credit reports and periods of unemployment that contributed to financial problems. Both also describe repayment or dispute efforts on some of the debts.

Both applicants are unmarried with no children, have worked for a defense contractor, and were alleged to have financial problems that raised questions about reliability and trustworthiness, with delinquent debts appearing on credit reports and the Government citing poor self-control and judgment. Both attributed their financial difficulties in part to periods of unemployment.
